claims.statement: For every hub-attached tree with path 0-1-2 and 1 to 5 branches, each branch center adjacent to 0 and having 2, 3, or 4 pendant leaves, every eligible lower-region rank in the specified exact finite census has S<0; no eligible row has a proper favorable-leaf selector or a positive local summand, and no whole-tree independence polynomial in this census fails coefficient log-concavity.
claims.scope: Exact bounded census of the 55 nondecreasing multisets of arities 2,3,4 of lengths 1 through 5, covering all ranks p with x+2<=p<=alpha and 3p<2alpha+1. This is computational evidence only and does not establish the heterogeneous extension or the universal primary claim.
claims.reason: Exact recurrence computation and an independent hub-factor coefficient formula agree on all 55 profiles. The finite result has no counterexample and supplies no general proof, mixed-selector witness, distributed marked-polynomial curvature theorem, or global D+C budget.

limitations: The graph family is restricted to a path 0-1-2 with 1 to 5 star branches at 0, each of arity 2, 3, or 4.
The finite census is not exhaustive over ordinary trees and cannot resolve the universal target.
Every eligible row in this family has all original leaves selected, so selector-change behavior was not tested.
Whole-tree coefficient log-concavity does not imply the proposed common-minor or distributed marked-polynomial inequalities.
No proof of the global D+C budget or of the heterogeneous extension is supplied.
